target.name: WISE 0855−0714
target.summary_plain: A free-floating brown dwarf about as cold as a winter day on Earth, 7.4 light-years away. It is invisible in ordinary light; SPHEREx only sees its faint glow at its longest infrared wavelengths, 4 to 5 microns.

astrometry.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7 (Spitzer; position at MJD 57633.39)

render.note: One asinh stretch per detector (0.5-99.7 percentiles of all its epochs), shared by every epoch, so brightness changes between frames are real. Co-adds: IMAGE minus ZODI, official photometry mask 0x3C028E44 rejected, OVERFLOW kept and flagged, then an inverse-variance mean after 3-sigma clipping (drops single-exposure streaks). Then vs Now: each image stretched by its own 0.5-99.7 percentiles. Differences: S/N, linear between the limits.

motion.method: Per-epoch D5+D6 co-adds; Gaussian PSF fit with the static CatWISE2020 neighbours modelled; errors from a bootstrap over exposures; parallax removed in the fit
motion.verdict_text: Between May 2025 and May 2026 the faint spot moved 8.0 ± 0.8″ toward PA 274°; the Spitzer astrometry predicts 8.0″ toward PA 275°. A static source is rejected at 10σ. Positions come from D5+D6 co-adds with the catalogued neighbour 4–11″ away modelled; the detection itself is weak (S/N about 8 per epoch).

notes: Each point is one exposure: forced photometry at the catalogue position (ePSF fit, or a fit to the PSF wings when the core is saturated).
Saturated points are shown hollow and excluded from fits.
The quick-look curve is the Year-1 spectral cube at 12.9″ pixels: it blends close neighbours, and channels where the star saturates are left empty.

warnings: Faint: S/N about 8 per epoch in the D5+D6 co-adds, below the a-priori 10. Invisible in D1–D4.
Blending: a catalogued star (W2 = 15.2) 4–11″ away overlaps it at SPHEREx resolution; it was modelled in the position fits, and dominates the D1–D4 images.
2 of 4 epochs are partial (fewer than 12 images per detector): shown greyed out.
False colour exists for 3 of 4 epochs: it needs D1, D3 and D6 in the same epoch.
